request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their statement as a CSV file: a header line
number,date,amount,figure,status then one line per claim of theirs bound by their last statement,
oldest first, with the bound figure as the claim shows it.

agent.result_text:
I added the statement export button. Three of the four tests pass; **"statement export scenario 3" still fails**. The failing check is about the rate calendar on a sheet viewed as of an earlier date, which as far as I can tell has nothing to do with the export, and I left it alone.

**The change** is one new file, `src/main/frontend/features/statements/exportStatement.slot.tsx`. It adds a "Statement export" column to each person's row with a `person-export-statement` button. Pressing it downloads `statement-<id>.csv`. That file starts with the header `number,date,amount,figure,status`, then has one line per claim the person's last statement bound, oldest first. The figure is the same one the claim's due cell shows. A person with no bound claims gets just the header. It reuses the existing CSV download helper and the figure logic from the claims export. No server or database change was needed, because claims already say whether the last statement bound them and at what figure.

**Why scenario 3 fails** (`acceptance.spec.ts:1530`): with the screen set as of 2026-03-20, the test expects `rate-month-A-2026-04` to show `12.50`, a rate that comes from the parent sheet. The app shows `n/a` instead. My reading of the code:
- The history log stamps each change with the sheet's own "today" (`history/Journal.java:66`), and falls back to the real date for a sheet that hasn't been stored.
- The test sets rates on the parent sheet without ever setting its today, so those rates are stamped with today's real date, 2026-10-30.
- Read as of 2026-03-20, the parent's rates don't exist yet, so the months that rely on them show `n/a`.

This probably passed when the test was written, while the real date was still before 2026-03-20. That would make it a clock-dependent failure that was already there. I tried to reproduce it directly with a few API calls, but setting the parent sheet didn't take, so I couldn't confirm it outside the test.

Getting it to pass would mean changing how parent-sheet rates are read in as-of mode, for example reading them as they are now. That changes behaviour for real users. Since it's outside this request, I'd rather you decide whether to do it. I can make that change if you want.
